title: KIN-SYS Protocol: Provider-Neutral Governed Execution Prototype
description: KIN-SYS is a provider-neutral protocol architecture for governing and verifying digital instructions across institutional and jurisdictional boundaries. This 0.2.0 research/reference release extends the MINAH-first governed execution prototype with institutional deployment and lifecycle registries; tenant-scoped, versioned authority grants; receiver-controlled institutional trust; issuer-signed and receiver-accepted grant provenance; provider-neutral OIDC identity adapter contracts; PostgreSQL-backed federation inbox/outbox, replay protection, retry and signed acknowledgement flows; and cross-installation reference tests. The repository includes 789 conformance tests (4 skipped, 0 failures) on the merged main commit, a runnable local HTTP prototype, reproducible reports, and explicit architecture/security limitations. This is not a production deployment. Identity providers, legal-source verification, institutional evidence, key custody and external services still require institution-specific integration. The two-installation PostgreSQL tests use isolated databases but execute adapters in one process; the process-separated mTLS transport test uses a minimal receiver stub. Independent deployed hosts, live institutional OIDC, production key custody, production-grade tenant isolation, distributed finality and exactly-once external effects are not claimed.
